+# #2867 - Example case 3d/rest
+
+## Chosen
+
+- The case uses two 3D Pockets: a 12 mm end mill (`EM-1200-2FL`), then a
+  6 mm end mill (`EM-0600-4FL`). The second pocket is limited by the
+  re-machining mask: CamCraft simulates the program ahead and cuts only
+  where material still stands. No new parameter or code was needed.
+- The part is a plate with two ribs and an 8 mm channel between them. The
+  walls are vertical, so the 12 mm tool leaves a rest region with a clear
+  shape (the channel and its two mouths), and the 6 mm tool leaves no
+  thin skims on the outer walls.
+- The README shows the rest region as a text top view with coordinates.
+- The test `catalog_3d_rest::the_small_tool_cuts_only_the_rest_region` pins
+  the claim of the issue ("the second operation cuts only that region") on
+  the committed program.
+
+## Why
+
+- The earlier blocker note on #2867 said that no 3D operation has a
+  rest-stock input. The 3D Pocket reads the stock of the program ahead
+  (M3.1 D), which is rest machining by the previous operations. That is the
+  workflow of the case.
+- A height-field mesh with ramped walls leaves a small staircase on each
+  wall. The second pocket could then cut thin skims on all walls, and the
+  rest region would not be clear.
+
+## Dropped
+
+- `rest_rough` on the 3D Pocket. It closes the staircase of the same tool.
+  It is not a second, smaller tool.
+- Catalog screenshots (`cargo xtask catalog --screenshots`). The command
+  pushes to an images branch. The README text view and the pin show the
+  region without it.
+- A 3D Finish after the rest pass. The case shows rest machining only.
+  `3d/rough-finish` shows the finish operations.

+# Rest Machining (two 3D Pockets, 12 mm then 6 mm)
+
+A 60 x 50 x 4 mm clean-room aluminum plate with two parallel ribs on top.
+Each rib is 13 mm wide, 30 mm long and 10 mm high (top at `Z14`). The ribs
+stand at `X-17..-4` and `X4..17`, from `Y-15` to `Y15`. The channel between
+them is 8 mm wide. The stock is a 60 x 50 x 18 mm box (top at `Z18`).
+
+## What it shows
+
+1. **3D Pocket (`3D Pocket D12`, `EM-1200-2FL`):** Roughs the stock down to
+   the plate in 2 mm levels, with a 6 mm stepover and 0.2 mm stock to leave.
+   The levels are `Z16`, `Z14.2` (0.2 mm above the rib tops), `Z14`, `Z12`,
+   `Z10`, `Z8`, `Z6` and `Z4.2` (0.2 mm above the plate). The 12 mm tool
+   plus 0.2 mm on each side needs 12.4 mm, so it cannot go into the 8 mm
+   channel below the rib tops.
+2. **3D Pocket (`3D Pocket D6 rest`, `EM-0600-4FL`):** The same pocket with a
+   6 mm tool. CamCraft simulates the program ahead of it and cuts only where
+   material still stands (re-machining). This operation has no rest switch:
+   the stock of the earlier operation limits it.
+
+## The rest region
+
+The 12 mm pass leaves this material, seen from the top (`#` is a rib, `R`
+is the rest region):
+
+```text
+  Y
+  25 +-------------------------------------------+
+     |                                           |
+  15 |      +---------+ R R R +---------+        |
+     |      |#########|R R R R|#########|        |
+     |      |#########|R R R R|#########|        |
+     |      |#########|R R R R|#########|        |
+ -15 |      +---------+ R R R +---------+        |
+     |                                           |
+ -25 +-------------------------------------------+
+    -30    -17       -4   0   4        17       30  X
+```
+
+- In the channel: `X-4..4`, `Y-15..15`, from `Z14.2` down to the plate.
+- At the two mouths of the channel (`Y` near `-15` and `15`): the corners
+  next to the rib ends that the 12 mm radius cannot reach.
+
+The 6 mm operation cuts only there. All its feed moves have the tool centre
+inside `X-2.2..2.2`, `Y-17.7..17.7`. Between the ribs the centre stays inside
+`X-0.79..0.79`: 3 mm tool radius plus 0.2 mm stock to leave from each wall.
+The test `catalog_3d_rest::the_small_tool_cuts_only_the_rest_region` pins
+this on the committed program.
+
+## What to look at
+
+- NC line 1573 starts `3D Pocket D6 rest`. It has no level at `Z16`: the
+  12 mm tool cleared it. Its first level is at `Z14`, in the channel only.
+  Its last level, at `Z4.2`, starts at NC line 2580.
+- The 6 mm program is 1,421 mm of cut, about 1.7 minutes. The 12 mm program
+  is 7,581 mm, about 7.8 minutes. The rest pass does not cut the large open
+  areas again.
+- The two operations report `entry:` notes. The helix and the ramp do not
+  fit at some pass starts, so they ramp along the pass.
+- `cam.verify()` must report no finding before the post. The script stops
+  if it does.
+
+## Files
+
+- `model/gen_rest_obj.py` — generator for the watertight test solid (a plate
+  with two ribs, vertical walls).
+- `model/rest.obj` — generated triangle mesh imported by `build.camscript`.
+- `build.camscript` — headless script that builds `rest.camproj` and posts
+  `rest.nc` through CamCraft's undoable commands.
+- `rest.camproj` — committed project with generated toolpaths.
+- `rest.nc` — committed Fanuc NC program, verified byte for byte in
+  `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs`.
+
+## Rebuild and verify
+
+From the repository root:
+
+```sh
+cargo xtask catalog --case 3d/rest
+cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog catalog_3d_rest
+```

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Regenerate rest.obj, the model of the catalog case 3d/rest.
+
+The part is an original CamCraft fixture: a 60 x 50 x 4 mm plate with two
+parallel ribs on top. Each rib is 13 mm wide (X), 30 mm long (Y) and 10 mm
+high, so its top is at Z14. The ribs stand at X -17..-4 and X 4..17. The
+channel between them is 8 mm wide: a 12 mm end mill cannot enter it, a
+6 mm end mill can.
+
+Method: the top is a set of flat rectangles on the rectilinear grid of the
+feature breakpoints. Each cell is the plate top (Z4) or a rib top (Z14).
+Where two neighbour cells have different heights, a vertical wall joins
+them. Four side walls and a bottom fan (Z0) close the solid. The script
+checks that each edge is used exactly twice, in opposite directions,
+before it writes.
+
+Usage: python gen_rest_obj.py [output.obj]
+"""
+
+import sys
+
+XS = [-30.0, -17.0, -4.0, 4.0, 17.0, 30.0]   # plate edges and rib walls
+YS = [-25.0, -15.0, 15.0, 25.0]              # plate edges and rib ends
+PLATE = 4.0                                  # plate top
+RIB = 14.0                                   # rib top
+
+
+def cell_height(i, j):
+    """Top Z of grid cell (i, j): the ribs are cells X 1 and 3, Y 1."""
+    return RIB if i in (1, 3) and j == 1 else PLATE
+
+
+def build():
+    nx, ny = len(XS) - 1, len(YS) - 1
+    tris = []
+
+    def quad(a, b, c, d):
+        tris.extend([(a, b, c), (a, c, d)])
+
+    # Cell tops, counter-clockwise from +Z.
+    for i in range(nx):
+        for j in range(ny):
+            z = cell_height(i, j)
+            x0, x1, y0, y1 = XS[i], XS[i + 1], YS[j], YS[j + 1]
+            quad((x0, y0, z), (x1, y0, z), (x1, y1, z), (x0, y1, z))
+    # Vertical walls between neighbour cells of different heights. The
+    # wall faces the low cell.
+    for i in range(nx - 1):
+        for j in range(ny):
+            za, zb = cell_height(i, j), cell_height(i + 1, j)
+            if za == zb:
+                continue
+            x, y0, y1 = XS[i + 1], YS[j], YS[j + 1]
+            if za < zb:   # wall faces -X
+                quad((x, y1, za), (x, y0, za), (x, y0, zb), (x, y1, zb))
+            else:         # wall faces +X
+                quad((x, y0, zb), (x, y1, zb), (x, y1, za), (x, y0, za))
+    for i in range(nx):
+        for j in range(ny - 1):
+            za, zb = cell_height(i, j), cell_height(i, j + 1)
+            if za == zb:
+                continue
+            y, x0, x1 = YS[j + 1], XS[i], XS[i + 1]
+            if za < zb:   # wall faces -Y
+                quad((x0, y, za), (x1, y, za), (x1, y, zb), (x0, y, zb))
+            else:         # wall faces +Y
+                quad((x1, y, zb), (x0, y, zb), (x0, y, za), (x1, y, za))
+    # Side walls and bottom fan: walk the boundary counter-clockwise seen
+    # from +Z. The boundary cells are all plate cells (Z4).
+    ring = ([(XS[i], YS[0]) for i in range(nx)] + [(XS[nx], YS[j]) for j in range(ny)]
+            + [(XS[i], YS[ny]) for i in range(nx, 0, -1)] + [(XS[0], YS[j]) for j in range(ny, 0, -1)])
+    centre = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
+    for n, (x0, y0) in enumerate(ring):
+        x1, y1 = ring[(n + 1) % len(ring)]
+        quad((x0, y0, 0.0), (x1, y1, 0.0), (x1, y1, PLATE), (x0, y0, PLATE))
+        tris.append((centre, (x1, y1, 0.0), (x0, y0, 0.0)))   # faces -Z
+    return tris
+
+
+def check(tris):
+    edges = {}
+    for t in tris:
+        for n in range(3):
+            e = (t[n], t[(n + 1) % 3])
+            edges[e] = edges.get(e, 0) + 1
+    for (p, q), count in edges.items():
+        if count != 1 or edges.get((q, p)) != 1:
+            raise SystemExit(f"mesh is not closed at edge {p} -> {q}")
+
+
+def write(tris, path):
+    verts, index, faces = [], {}, []
+    for t in tris:
+        face = []
+        for p in t:
+            if p not in index:
+                index[p] = len(verts) + 1
+                verts.append(p)
+            face.append(index[p])
+        faces.append(face)
+    with open(path, "w", newline="\n") as f:
+        f.write("# rest: 60 x 50 x 4 mm plate with two 13 x 30 x 10 mm ribs and an 8 mm channel\n")
+        for v in verts:
+            f.write("v {:g} {:g} {:g}\n".format(*v))
+        for face in faces:
+            f.write("f " + " ".join(str(n) for n in face) + "\n")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    out = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "rest.obj"
+    mesh = build()
+    check(mesh)
+    write(mesh, out)
